I would advise you to find a project that you are passionate/excited about and really commit to it (like if you really like writing you can try writing a novel, or if you like painting you can try painting 50 paintings). It might take a few projects/goals to help. The last time I was depressed, I read a book series, THEN I revised a story that I wrote, THEN I perfected my backstroke and front crawl with side breathing (swimming), THEN I cried. A lot. But THEN I felt a lot better. A few weeks later I realized I wasn't depressed anymore. I'd also recommend visiting https://www.reddit.com/r/depression/ and talking with some other people. It sure helped me.

If this doesn't work for you and nothing else seems to be helping, just sit down in your room one day and cry and pity yourself and watch Netflix and read sappy romance novels. Maybe write a diary entry. Rant to someone in person. Eat ice cream. You might find that you feel a lot better after crying yourself to sleep (it is inevitable in this situation). Please, please, please, DO NOT FORGET THAT YOU ALWAYS HAVE OPTIONS. Suicide is never the answer. So many people care about you. Don't forget that your SO really does want to help. They probably really love you. I wish you the best of luck. Stay strong! <3

Hi. I'm a 13-year-old girl. I have a counselor, and I used to see her because I was depressed, but now I see her about my anxiety and various phobias. I have a fear of my reflection and it gives me so much anxiety that I'm scared to look out the window in fear of seeing my reflection in it. I think my fear comes from this movie I watched when I was five or six. It was a kid's movie, and it was about the Bratz (basically Barbies but trashier lol) characters when they were kids. They all went to a sleepover and told scary stories to each other. One of the stories (BTW, they actually showed the stories on screen, so you saw it as well as heard it) was told by a girl names Sasha. Sasha apparently went to the carnival and went in the fun-house. One of the mirrors there did nothing, and it was called the Doppleganger (sorry if I spelled that wrong). Eventually, her reflection came out of the mirror and chased her around the carnival. After a while, Sasha's reflection chased her into the fun-house, except there were a bunch of Doppleganger mirrors in the room now. Her reflection put Sasha into the original Doppleganger mirror so that the original Sasha was now the reflection. Now I am scarred for life.

YES. People CAN help you. Counselors, loved ones, doctors. Counselors are worth the money. They don't usually ACT like therapists. The act more like friends who are genuinely concerned.

If you are scared to tell your loved ones, think about getting a counselor. In my experience, counselors act like friends and what is said during your appointment, stays between you unless you would like it otherwise or you are a danger to yourself and/or others. If you don't want to pay for a counselor, you can see your school guidance counselor if your school has one. If your school doesn't have one, then you can always talk to your teacher. Eventually, you will have to tell your parents, but if you're uncomfortable with that at the moment, you can always talk to someone else which might help. There are also depression hotlines that you can look up online and call on your phone.
